nodes.title: Ndea
nodes.description: AGI lab merging deep learning with program synthesis — a direct bet against the scaling hypothesis. $43M raised. YC W26.
nodes.body:
**Website:** ndea.com | **Twitter:** @ndea | **YC slug:** ndea-com

Founded by [Francois Chollet](./Francois%20Chollet.md) and [Mike Knoop](./Mike%20Knoop.md). Team of 15. YC partner: Tyler Bosmeny.

Entered YC W26 having already raised **$43M** — the largest pre-program raise in the entire batch. Goal: create a "factory for rapid scientific advancement" capable of autonomous invention and discovery across drug discovery, robotics, energy, and space.

Ndea's thesis diverges sharply from the mainstream scaling consensus. Where frontier labs bet on larger models trained on more data, Ndea bets on **program synthesis**: systems that discover and compose explicit programs to solve problems, rather than pattern-matching from training data.

Chollet and Knoop are also co-founders of the ARC Prize Foundation — offering $1M annual prizes for AI systems that pass the ARC-AGI benchmark, a test that current LLMs consistently fail. Ndea is the commercial expression of that conviction.

[Synthetic Sciences](./Synthetic%20Sciences.md) and [Origin Bio](./Origin%20Bio.md) operate in the same AI-for-science space from different angles; Ndea's contribution is the foundational model architecture rather than the application layer.

_Avoid:_ Treating Ndea as another LLM startup. They are explicitly building something orthogonal to the transformer scaling paradigm.

_Usage:_

"Is Ndea competing with OpenAI and Anthropic?"

"Not directly. They're betting the path to AGI runs through program synthesis, not scaling transformers. If they're right, the frontier labs are optimising the wrong variable."

nodes.title: Synthetic Sciences
nodes.description: Infrastructure for scientific superintelligence — AI co-scientists for full research workflows. 92% on BixBench. YC W26.
nodes.body:
**Website:** syntheticsciences.ai | **Twitter:** @SynScience | **GitHub:** github.com/synthetic-sciences | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/company/synsci

Founded by [Aayam Bansal](./Aayam%20Bansal.md) and [Ishaan Gangwani](./Ishaan%20Gangwani.md). Team of 2. YC partner: Gustaf Alstromer. Backed by a16z Scout Fund ($1.4M pre-YC + $500K YC = $1.9M total).

Scored **92% on BixBench** — a biology-specific reasoning benchmark. "Claude Code for science."

Enables AI co-scientists to autonomously handle: literature synthesis, hypothesis generation, experiment design, code execution, data analysis, and publication-ready output. High-fidelity evaluations and RL environments for long-horizon scientific research.

The founding age (both ~18) is a data point, not a gimmick. Gangwani is International Olympiad in AI 2025 (Honorable Mention), USACO Platinum (top 0.01% globally). Bansal has published at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAA, CVPR — rare credentials for any founder, exceptional for an 18-year-old.

Both are Z-Fellows and Emergent Ventures recipients — independent signals of exceptional technical ability.

[Ndea](./Ndea.md) bets on the model architecture layer; Synthetic Sciences bets on the application layer that makes AI agents do real scientific work now, with existing models.

_Usage:_

"Is this just a paper-reading assistant?"

"No. The agents run full research workflows — designing experiments, analysing results, synthesising across literature. The 92% BixBench score suggests it handles non-trivial biological reasoning."

nodes.title: Origin Bio
nodes.description: DNA foundation model that outperforms DeepMind's AlphaGenome on genomic benchmarks. YC W26.
nodes.body:
Origin Bio built a foundation model trained on genomic sequences that, according to benchmark results, outperforms DeepMind's AlphaGenome on several genomic understanding tasks. The model predicts gene expression, regulatory element activity, and other molecular phenotypes from DNA sequence alone.

The company sits in the same wave as [Synthetic Sciences](./Synthetic%20Sciences.md) — using foundation model architectures trained on biological data to accelerate scientific discovery. Where Synthetic Sciences automates research workflows, Origin Bio provides the predictive model layer for genomics.

The AlphaGenome comparison is the key credibility marker: DeepMind's genomics group is one of the best-resourced in the world. Beating their published benchmarks from a seed-stage YC company is either a strong result or a sign that the benchmark framing matters as much as the score.

_Usage:_

"What does outperforming AlphaGenome actually mean?"

"It means Origin Bio's model predicts gene expression from DNA sequence more accurately on the held-out test sets the benchmark uses. Whether those test sets generalize to real biology is the open question."

Directed toward the grand challenges of biology and materials science. Mission: build the machine that discovers the next Transformer, the next AlphaFold, and the breakthroughs that push science and engineering to the absolute frontier.

nodes.title: Multifactor
nodes.description: Zero-trust auth and authorization for AI agents with patented prompt injection defense. $15M raised. YC F25.
nodes.body:
**Website:** multifactor.com | **Twitter:** @multifactorcom | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/company/multifactorcom

Founded by [Vivek Nair](./Vivek%20Nair.md) and [Colin Roberts](./Colin%20Roberts.md). San Francisco. Team of 6. YC partner: Nicolas Dessaigne.

Raised **$15M** — largest funding round in the F25 batch. Vivek Nair turned down substantial VC term sheets to go through YC instead.

Enterprise customers include manufacturing supply chain operators managing **$7.5B+** in assets.

Provides fine-grained, auditable, zero-trust authentication specifically for AI agents: "checkpoint links" that let agents share online accounts without exposing passwords, with patented defense against prompt injection attacks.

When an agent calls an API or executes a database query, existing systems either grant it full user permissions (too broad) or no permissions (useless). Multifactor provides per-operation authorization with audit trails — the security primitive the agentic stack was missing.

Natural stack with [Metorial](./Metorial.md) (agent-to-tool connections) and [Browser Use](./Browser%20Use.md) (browser control) — Metorial routes agents, Multifactor controls what agents are authorized to do, Browser Use executes.

_Usage:_

"Can't I just use OAuth for agent auth?"

"OAuth works for humans following an interactive login flow. Agents run headlessly, often calling thousands of APIs per session. You need per-operation authorization with audit trails, not a token granting broad access for 24 hours."

nodes.title: Metorial
nodes.description: Enterprise MCP platform connecting Claude Code, Cursor and 600+ integrations with sub-second boot. "Vercel for MCP." YC F25.
nodes.body:
**Website:** metorial.com | **Twitter:** @MetorialAi | **GitHub:** github.com/metorial | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/company/metorial

Founded by [Karim Rahme](./Karim%20Rahme.md) and [Tobias Herber](./Tobias%20Herber.md). Vienna, Austria. Team of 4.

Flagship product **Magic MCP** connects MCP clients — Cursor, Claude Code, Claude Desktop — to 600+ integrations with enterprise-grade security, scaling, observability, and sub-second boot times.

MCP (Model Context Protocol, released by Anthropic) is the emerging standard for how AI agents connect to external tools and APIs. Metorial provides the serverless runtime layer: idle servers hibernate and resume with sub-second cold starts, connections are secured and monitored, enterprise compliance requirements are met.

The Vercel analogy is precise: Vercel didn't invent deployment, it made Next.js reliable at enterprise scale. Metorial does the same for MCP — the protocol exists and works at small scale; Metorial makes it work where enterprises require it.

Natural stack with [Multifactor](./Multifactor.md) (what agents are allowed to do) and [Browser Use](./Browser%20Use.md) (how agents control browsers). [S2](./S2.md) handles the streaming data layer beneath.

_Usage:_

"Why not run MCP servers yourself?"

"You can, until you need multi-region failover, SOC2 compliance, audit logs, and 99.9% uptime SLAs. That's what Metorial provides on top of the open protocol."

nodes.title: RunAnywhere
nodes.description: Fastest on-device AI inference for Apple Silicon, beating Apple's MLX. 10K GitHub stars. YC W26.
nodes.body:
**Website:** runanywhere.ai | **Docs:** docs.runanywhere.ai | **GitHub:** RunanywhereAI/runanywhere-sdks (10,100+ stars)

Founded by [Sanchit Monga](./Sanchit%20Monga.md) and [Shubham Malhotra](./Shubham%20Malhotra.md). San Francisco. Team of 5.

Inference engine for Apple Silicon that outperforms Apple's own MLX framework. Single SDK for multimodal AI models running fully on-device, with a central control plane for model rollouts, versioning, and access policies across thousands of devices — no cloud required.

Shubham Malhotra built MetalRT — the first complete multimodal inference engine for Apple Silicon — before RunAnywhere. That specific prior work is the technical moat: most founders approaching on-device AI don't have GPU kernel optimisation experience. Malhotra does.

Sanchit Monga comes from Intuit where he built mobile SDKs used by 50M+ active users. The combination of kernel-level performance expertise (Malhotra) and SDK distribution experience (Monga) is the right founding pair for this product.

The 10K GitHub stars at seed stage places RunAnywhere alongside [Browser Use](./Browser%20Use.md) as one of the most developer-resonant W25/W26 launches.

_Usage:_

"Why does Apple Silicon need a third-party inference engine?"

"MLX is general-purpose and evolves slowly. RunAnywhere specialises for inference throughput and can iterate faster — same reason NVIDIA's cuDNN gets beat by specialised kernels in certain workloads."

nodes.title: S2
nodes.description: Serverless API for streaming real-time data to collaborative AI applications. YC F25.
nodes.body:
Founded by Stephen Balogh, Shikhar Bhushan, and Dwarak Govind Parthiban. Raised $3.85M. Builds the infrastructure layer for streaming data feeds — real-time events that collaborative and agentic applications need to stay in sync across users and agents simultaneously.

The problem: as AI applications become multi-agent and collaborative, the data transport layer matters as much as the model. WebSockets and polling were built for simpler use cases. S2 provides a serverless, globally distributed streaming primitive designed for the latency and reliability requirements of AI workloads.

Comparable positioning to how [Byteport](./Byteport.md) solves the network transport problem and [Metorial](./Metorial.md) solves the agent connection problem — S2 solves the data stream problem in the same emerging AI infrastructure stack.

_Usage:_

"Can't I just use WebSockets?"

"For low-traffic apps, yes. When you have thousands of agents and users sharing live state — collaborative editing, multi-agent coordination, real-time analytics — you need global distribution, backpressure handling, and durability guarantees that WebSockets don't provide."

nodes.title: Byteport
nodes.description: File transfer protocol delivering 10x faster speeds than TCP, 1000x improvement on unreliable networks. YC W26.
nodes.body:
Built a new file transfer protocol that claims 10x faster speeds than TCP under normal conditions and 1000x improvement on unreliable, high-latency networks. TCP's congestion control algorithm was designed in 1988 for a world of wired connections; it performs poorly on satellite, mobile, and international links.

The benchmark claims are large enough to be skeptical of until independently verified — but the problem space is real. QUIC (used in HTTP/3) already demonstrated that TCP's assumptions are limiting. Byteport is betting that file transfer specifically has worse assumptions and more room to improve than general web traffic.

Practical applications: large model downloads, training data transfers, cross-region backup, multi-site content delivery. All of these are bottlenecked by the same TCP assumptions that Byteport targets.

Sits alongside [RunAnywhere](./RunAnywhere.md) and [S2](./S2.md) in the AI infrastructure layer — all three making the physical movement of data faster and more reliable as AI workloads demand more of the network.

_Usage:_

"Is this just a different TCP implementation?"

"It's a different congestion control approach at the transport layer, optimized for large file transfers rather than general web traffic. The gains come from not sharing TCP's conservative assumptions about what the network can handle."

nodes.title: LunaBill
nodes.description: AI voice agents that handle medical billing calls with EHR integration and HIPAA compliance. YC F25.
nodes.body:
Founded by Suhail Parry and David Day. Builds AI voice agents specifically for the medical billing call category — insurance authorization calls, claim follow-ups, prior authorization requests, and patient payment conversations.

Medical billing calls are a $25B+ industry in the US: hospitals employ thousands of billing staff whose job is to call insurance companies, navigate phone trees, wait on hold, and dispute denials. Each call follows predictable scripts but requires real-time adaptation when the insurance agent asks unexpected questions. LunaBill automates the routine calls and flags complex ones for human review.

The HIPAA compliance and EHR integration are the technical moat: connecting to Epic, Cerner, or Athenahealth requires security certifications and integration work that competitors can't bypass. Once a hospital system has integrated and validated the product, switching costs are high.

Positioned alongside [Beacon Health](./Beacon%20Health.md) in the healthcare AI automation space — [Beacon Health](./Beacon%20Health.md) handles clinical workflows within EHR systems, LunaBill handles the financial workflows that happen outside them.

_Usage:_

"Why can't hospitals just train staff better instead of using AI for billing calls?"

"Staff turnover in medical billing is 30-40% annually. Every new hire requires months of training. AI agents don't quit, don't need training resets, and can handle 10x the call volume of a human team."

Founded by [Lucas Ngoo](./Lucas%20Ngoo.md). Raised $6M. Builds high-quality training datasets for embodied AI — specifically egocentric video (first-person perspective) and robot data captured in real workplace environments, with hand and body pose annotations.

The training data bottleneck for robotics is acute: robots need to learn from demonstrations, but demonstration data is expensive, hard to collect, and usually captured in sterile lab environments. Cortex AI captures data in real factories, warehouses, and workplaces — messier but more representative of actual deployment conditions.

The annotation layer (hand pose, body pose, object interaction) is what separates Cortex AI from raw video: annotated data is what robots can actually learn from.

Sits in the same data infrastructure layer as [Ndea](./Ndea.md)'s training data philosophy — both companies believe the quality and type of training data matters as much as the architecture of the model being trained.

_Usage:_

"Isn't synthetic data replacing real demonstrations for robot training?"

"Not yet at the manipulation skill level. Synthetic data works for navigation; for fine manipulation tasks — screwing a bolt, folding fabric — real demonstration data still produces better policies."

nodes.title: SolidRoad
nodes.description: AI training and QA platform for customer experience agents. $6.5M seed → $25M Series A. YC W25.
nodes.body:
**Website:** solidroad.com | **Twitter:** @markhuqhes (CEO) | **YC partner:** Brad Flora

Founded by [Mark Hughes](./Mark%20Hughes.md) and [Patrick Finlay](./Patrick%20Finlay.md). San Francisco. Team of 6.

**$6.5M seed** (June 2025) → **$25M Series A** (April 2026). Real production results: 50% reduction in onboarding times at PartnerHero and Tech Mahindra; +3% go-live CSAT at Crypto.com (above 90%).

Companies deploying AI agents for customer service have no systematic way to test them. Human QA doesn't scale — you'd need as many reviewers as conversations. SolidRoad automates the QA layer: synthetic adversarial test conversations, failure mode identification, performance scoring, and automatic training data generation from regressions.

The loop: deploy agent → SolidRoad finds failures → failures become training examples → agent improves → repeat.

The $25M Series A in April 2026 — less than a year after a $6.5M seed — is one of the fastest institutional re-ups in the F25/W25 cohort. It reflects real enterprise traction, not just Demo Day momentum.

Sits in a natural stack with [Multifactor](./Multifactor.md) (agent security) and [Metorial](./Metorial.md) (agent connections). Where [Bolna](./Bolna.md) and [Beacon Health](./Beacon%20Health.md) deploy agents into verticals, SolidRoad is the horizontal QA layer any deployment needs.

_Usage:_

"Can't I just monitor customer satisfaction scores?"

"CSAT is lagging — you find out the agent failed after the customer had a bad experience. SolidRoad catches failures before real users hit them by running adversarial test cases against the agent in simulation."

nodes.title: Flick AI
nodes.description: AI-powered canvas for video creation and editing with an intuitive visual interface. YC F25.
nodes.body:
Founded by Ray Wang and Zoey Zhang. Raised $6M. Builds an AI-native video creation interface — a canvas-based editor where users can generate, edit, and combine video clips using natural language and visual drag-and-drop, rather than traditional timeline-based editing.

The positioning targets the creator and marketing space: video content is the highest-engagement format but has the highest production barrier. Professional video editors work in Premiere or Final Cut — tools that require years of skill investment. Flick AI targets the gap between "I want to make a video" and "I can afford/learn professional tools."

The canvas metaphor (rather than timeline) is the key UX bet: Figma proved that canvas interfaces unlock creative workflows that linear tools miss. Flick AI is testing whether that insight transfers to video.

Competes in the same creator tooling space as [Cardboard](./Cardboard.md), which takes a browser-native agentic approach to video editing rather than a canvas approach.

_Usage:_

"How is this different from CapCut or Adobe Express?"

"CapCut is template-based; Premiere is professional-grade. Flick AI is AI-first — the editing operations themselves are expressed in natural language, not manual timeline cuts. Different workflow, not a feature upgrade."

nodes.title: Beacon Health
nodes.description: AI employees for primary care — automates screenings, referrals, and authorizations inside EHRs. $5.4M from Accel + Sequoia. YC W26.
nodes.body:
**Website:** beaconhealth.ai | **YC partner:** Diana Hu

Founded by [Mark Pothen](./Mark%20Pothen.md) and [Obinna Akahara](./Obinna%20Akahara.md). San Francisco. Backed pre-YC by Accel and Sequoia scouts.

Raised **$5.4M** pre-YC. Currently operational with an IPA supporting **40,000 patients**.

AI agents working inside existing EHR (Electronic Health Record) systems to automate administrative tasks that consume 2+ hours of a physician's day: quality gap closures, risk adjustment, patient outreach, prior authorization requests, referral coordination, and follow-up scheduling.

The physician co-founder (Pothen) grew up in his mother's primary care practice and spent 6 months embedded in a clinic implementing AI before founding the company. That depth of clinical workflow understanding is what makes EHR integration decisions that outsider founders miss — and what makes the clinical trust required for adoption possible.

The Accel and Sequoia pre-YC backing signals institutional due diligence had already validated the team on clinical validity before YC added its check.

Works alongside [LunaBill](./LunaBill.md) in healthcare AI: [LunaBill](./LunaBill.md) handles the financial layer (billing calls outside EHR), Beacon Health handles the clinical administrative layer inside the EHR.

_Usage:_

"How did a startup get EHR access?"

"Slowly. Pothen's clinical background and 6-month clinic embedding built the relationships before the company existed. The Accel/Sequoia backing then accelerated the certification process."

nodes.title: Fort
nodes.description: Strength tracking wearable that measures muscle force directly during workouts. YC W26.
nodes.body:
Builds a wearable sensor system that measures actual muscle force output during strength training — not reps counted via accelerometer, not heart rate, but the actual contractile force that determines whether a workout stimulus is effective.

The technical distinction matters: two people performing the same exercise with the same weight can produce dramatically different muscle force outputs depending on tempo, range of motion, and neuromuscular activation. Existing wearables (Apple Watch, Whoop, Garmin) measure external proxies. Fort measures the signal that actually determines training adaptation.

The product reached 1,295 Twitter likes at launch — high for a fitness hardware company, suggesting genuine community interest from strength training enthusiasts who have been frustrated by the shallow data from existing wearables.

Competes for the same serious athlete audience as [Pocket](./Pocket.md) competes for the professional audience — both bet that a purpose-built hardware device extracts more value than a phone app trying to do the same thing.

_Usage:_

"How does Fort measure muscle force without being invasive?"

"Surface EMG (electromyography) — electrodes on skin detect the electrical signals that precede muscle contraction, which correlate with force output. The challenge is signal noise and calibration, which is where Fort's hardware differentiation lives."

nodes.title: GrazeMate
nodes.description: AI-powered autonomous drones for cattle management at scale. YC W26.
nodes.body:
Builds autonomous drone systems that monitor cattle herds across large grazing areas — tracking individual animals, detecting health issues, managing grazing rotation, and providing the livestock data that ranchers currently collect on horseback or ATVs.

Cattle ranching across the US involves monitoring animals spread across tens of thousands of acres. A rancher with 500 head of cattle can spend hours daily on patrol that produces limited data. GrazeMate replaces that patrol with continuous autonomous coverage and computer vision identification of each animal.

The practical problems being solved: early disease detection (an animal behaving differently before showing physical symptoms), grazing rotation optimization (moving herds before pasture is overgrazed), and accurate headcount (theft and stray detection).

The market is large and ignored: US cattle industry is $100B+, technology adoption is low, and precision agriculture software has focused on crops, not livestock.

1,210 Twitter likes at launch — high engagement for an agricultural tech product, suggesting significant rancher interest in the category.

GrazeMate sits in the same W26 hardware cluster as [Pocket](./Pocket.md) and [Fort](./Fort.md) — all three bet that purpose-built physical devices extract value that software-only solutions can't reach.

_Usage:_

"Drones and cattle seem like they'd conflict — wouldn't the animals spook?"

"Habituated drones flying at altitude don't spook cattle after a few exposures. The data quality gain is worth the adaptation period. Early ranch pilots confirmed cattle acclimate within a week."

nodes.title: OctaPulse
nodes.description: CV and robotics to automate quality inspection in fish farms. YC W26.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.tryoctapulse.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/octapulse

OctaPulse uses AI vision to automate hatchery QA for fish farms, starting with broodstock phenotyping and juvenile deformity inspection. OctaPulse cuts inspection time from about 5 minutes to under 30 seconds per fish, with more than 90 percent accuracy, so farms advance only high quality fish and waste less feed and labor. Its goal is to bring automation across the entire fish production lifecycle for the $300B aquaculture industry.

Aquaculture is the fastest growing food sector, and has already surpassed commercial fishing for production of seafood. Yet two of the most critical QA and QC steps in fish production are still done by hand: phenotyping and deformity inspection. These processes are slow, error prone, and despised by technicians but vital for the success of the farm, so much so that farms spend >$200K a year on trained technicians and geneticists to operate. We’ve built an AI vision platform for vertically integrated finfish farms that drops into existing workflows starting in the hatchery, uses off the shelf cameras, standardizes these QA steps, and creates a proprietary multi species dataset that becomes the brain for future autonomous aquafarms. Phenotyping is the start, but the platform is designed to be a drop in solution that can easily expand into feeding, health monitoring, and processing so it cans solve production problems across the lifecycle.

It signeds a 6-figure paid pilot with the largest trout producer in the United States, are deploying into 2 more farms early 2026, and trained models above 90 percent accuracy while cutting inspection time from 5 minutes to under 30 seconds. Each deployment adds labeled images to its dataset and improves cross species generalization.

Today, improving a VLA often means more real-world hours: setting up the scene, running trials, resetting, and repeating. This loop is slow, expensive, and hard to scale. nodes.title: GRU Space
nodes.description: First commercial lunar hotel — taking reservations for stays on the Moon. YC W26.
nodes.body:
Founded solo by [Skyler Chan](./Skyler%20Chan.md), age 22. Currently accepting reservations at $250K–$1M per stay. The only YC company in the W26 batch building commercial lunar hospitality infrastructure.

GRU Space's thesis: the Moon will have permanent human presence within a decade (via NASA's Artemis program, SpaceX, and commercial partners), and the hospitality infrastructure — safe, comfortable, commercially operated habitats — is a separate problem from the rocket and lander problem that governments and large primes are solving.

The business model mirrors early commercial aviation: sell experiences to wealthy early adopters, use that revenue to fund infrastructure that eventually enables broader access. The $250K–$1M price point targets the same customer who buys a Virgin Galactic ticket, not the general public.

At YC demo day, GRU Space had the highest novelty premium of the batch — the kind of audacious bet that generates coverage regardless of near-term revenue. Whether it's viable depends entirely on the pace of lunar infrastructure development from SpaceX and NASA.

**Website:** paxhistoria.co | **LinkedIn:** company page | **YC partner:** Harshita Arora

Founded by Eli Bullock-Papa and Ryan Zhang ("I like history"). Team of 3. San Francisco.

**35,000 daily active users**. 4,000+ published community presets (each with 50+ plays). **100 billion+ tokens processed weekly** — one of the highest token volumes in the W26 batch.

Players choose a country and historical moment — ancient Rome, Edo Japan, the French Revolution, "What if the USSR hadn't broken apart?" — and interact with a generatively simulated world populated by AI agents with historically grounded behaviour. [Synthetic Sciences](./Synthetic%20Sciences.md) simulates scientific research with AI agents. Pax Historia simulates historical societies. The shared architecture insight: LLMs are finally capable enough to maintain coherent, complex simulation state across long sessions.

nodes.title: Skillsync
nodes.description: Hiring platform that evaluates engineers on shipped work rather than resumes and interviews. YC W26.
nodes.body:
Reached 1,854 Twitter likes at launch. Builds an alternative hiring pipeline for engineers: instead of resumes, cover letters, and whiteboard interviews, candidates are evaluated on their actual shipped work — GitHub contributions, deployed projects, open-source impact, production code they can demonstrate.

The founding frustration: the resume + technical interview system selects for people who are good at passing technical interviews, which correlates imperfectly with people who are good at shipping software. Whiteboard coding in 45 minutes on an artificial problem is a poor proxy for the skills that matter in a real engineering role.

Skillsync's alternative: structured portfolios of real work, async technical demonstrations on actual problems, and employer-side tools to evaluate authentic engineering output.

The supply side (engineers) find it attractive because their actual work is being evaluated. The demand side (employers) find it attractive if they've been burned by interview-passing engineers who can't ship in production.

Skillsync and [Cardboard](./Cardboard.md) are both betting on work product over process — [Cardboard](./Cardboard.md) evaluates video through the actual editor experience, Skillsync evaluates engineers through their actual shipped code. [Pocket](./Pocket.md) produces the transcripts and notes that make work product visible after the fact.

_Usage:_

"Won't candidates just clean up their GitHub to look better?"

"Yes, and that's fine — curating your best work is a legitimate signal. It's still more predictive than optimizing for a specific LeetCode style in a 45-minute window."

Builds an alternative hiring pipeline for engineers: instead of resumes, cover letters, and whiteboard interviews, candidates are evaluated on their actual shipped work — GitHub contributions, deployed projects, open-source impact, production code they can demonstrate.

The founding frustration: the resume + technical interview system selects for people who are good at passing technical interviews, which correlates imperfectly with people who are good at shipping software. Whiteboard coding in 45 minutes on an artificial problem is a poor proxy for the skills that matter in a real engineering role.

Skillsync's alternative: structured portfolios of real work, async technical demonstrations on actual problems, and employer-side tools to evaluate authentic engineering output.

The supply side (engineers) find it attractive because their actual work is being evaluated. The demand side (employers) find it attractive if they've been burned by interview-passing engineers who can't ship in production.

Skillsync and [Cardboard](./Cardboard.md) are both betting on work product over process — [Cardboard](./Cardboard.md) evaluates video through the actual editor experience, Skillsync evaluates engineers through their actual shipped code. [Pocket](./Pocket.md) produces the transcripts and notes that make work product visible after the fact.
usage: Won't candidates just clean up their GitHub to look better?
Yes, and that's fine — curating your best work is a legitimate signal. It's still more predictive than optimizing for a specific LeetCode style in a 45-minute window.

BeeSafe AI is building the frontier model layer for social engineering defense. Cyberattacks have moved from code to conversation: attackers now use AI to carry out long-term, trust-based manipulation across SMS, voice, email, and social platforms, often inside encrypted channels where defenders cannot see, detect, or stop them.

BeeSafe changes that by deploying undercover AI agents that engage attackers directly, expose hidden infrastructure, and convert live adversarial conversations into actionable intelligence. Each engagement adds to BeeSafe's proprietary dataset of real attacker behavior and trains foundational models that continually learn about counter-persuasion, deception, and manipulation in the wild.

BeeSafe is starting in financial crime, where banks already value its data against Authorized Push Payment (APP) fraud and money laundering, but the opportunity is far broader. The same data and models that uncover mule networks today can protect consumers, secure enterprises, and strengthen governments against the next generation of AI-powered social engineering attacks tomorrow.

nodes.title: Francois Chollet
nodes.description: Creator of Keras, co-founder of Ndea and ARC Prize. The most credentialed ML researcher to bet against the scaling hypothesis.
nodes.body:
**Twitter:** @fchollet | **LinkedIn:** available

AI researcher at Google for a decade. Creator of **Keras** — the deep learning framework used by millions of practitioners globally, later integrated into TensorFlow as its official high-level API.

In 2019 published a landmark paper arguing that AI benchmarks measure memorisation and pattern matching, not genuine reasoning. Developed the **ARC-AGI benchmark** — tasks requiring visual reasoning and systematic generalisation that LLMs consistently fail.

Co-founded the **ARC Prize Foundation** with [Mike Knoop](./Mike%20Knoop.md) in 2024: $1M annual prizes for AI systems that pass ARC-AGI. The prize has driven significant research attention to the non-scaling approach to AGI.

Left Google in 2025 to co-found [Ndea](./Ndea.md) — an AGI lab pursuing program synthesis. The move was significant: Chollet had spent years publicly arguing that scaling was insufficient, then committed to building the alternative.

_Usage:_

"Is Chollet right that scaling won't reach AGI?"

"His ARC benchmark has proved resistant to LLMs for five years. Whether that resistance is fundamental or temporary is the exact bet that [Ndea](./Ndea.md) and the frontier labs are making on opposite sides."

nodes.title: Mike Knoop
nodes.description: Co-founder of Zapier and Ndea. Built a no-code unicorn, then pivoted to AGI research.
nodes.body:
**Twitter:** @mikeknoop | **Website:** mikeknoop.com | **LinkedIn:** available

Co-founded **Zapier** with Wade Foster and Bryan Helmig — the no-code automation platform that became the default glue layer between web apps. Reached $5B valuation as one of the few capital-efficient, bootstrapped unicorns in tech.

Left Zapier after 10+ years to co-found the **ARC Prize Foundation** with [Francois Chollet](./Francois%20Chollet.md): $1M annual prizes for AI systems that pass the ARC-AGI reasoning benchmark.

Co-founded [Ndea](./Ndea.md) with Chollet in 2025. Knoop brings what Chollet lacked: the operational experience of scaling a company from 0 to unicorn — building distributed teams, navigating product decisions, and managing the business challenges that pure researchers underestimate.

The Zapier background is directly relevant: Zapier was built on connecting things that weren't designed to talk to each other. Ndea's program synthesis approach — composing programs from components — maps to the same modularity instinct.

_Usage:_

"Why leave Zapier for AGI research?"

"He's said he believes AGI is one of the most important problems humanity faces. Once you believe that, staying to optimise a profitable no-code tool is the wrong allocation of time."

nodes.title: Akshay Narisetti
nodes.description: Co-founder and CEO of Pocket. Previously built Omi, an open-source AI note-taking device.
nodes.body:
**Twitter:** @AkshayNarisetti | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/akshaynarisetti

Co-founded [Pocket](./Pocket.md) with [Gabriel Dymowski](./Gabriel%20Dymowski.md).

Previously built **Omi** — an open-source AI note-taking device, which gave Narisetti direct experience with the hardware AI wearable space before Pocket. He knew the failure modes of previous devices (Humane AI Pin, Google Glass) from having shipped in the same category.

The $27M ARR in 5 months is the metric that defines his founding story: hardware velocity at that rate is essentially unprecedented in recent YC history. Series A-level traction at seed stage.

The prior Omi experience mattered: he didn't walk into hardware AI cold. He understood why previous devices failed (wrong form factor, wrong use case, wrong friction level) and designed Pocket around those lessons — smaller, more passive, solving one specific pain rather than replacing the phone.

_Usage:_

"What made Pocket succeed where Humane AI Pin failed?"

"Scope. Humane tried to replace the phone. Pocket has one job: capture the conversation you would have forgotten. The narrower the wedge, the clearer the value, the faster the adoption."

nodes.title: Colin Roberts
nodes.description: Co-founder and CTO of Multifactor. PhD mathematician, former NASA scientist, 10+ years cybersecurity.
nodes.body:
Co-founded [Multifactor](./Multifactor.md) with [Vivek Nair](./Vivek%20Nair.md).

**Ph.D. mathematician**. **Former NASA scientist**. 10+ years of professional cybersecurity experience.

The mathematical background is directly relevant to Multifactor's product: post-quantum cryptography — which Multifactor uses for its authentication system — is a field where mathematical depth determines whether the implementation is actually secure. A PhD mathematician with a decade of applied security experience is the right background for building cryptographic infrastructure that enterprises will stake their security posture on.

The NASA-to-cybersecurity-to-startup trajectory is unusual: deep technical credibility across high-stakes engineering domains, then applied to the commercial problem of securing AI agents. Roberts brings the theoretical rigour that makes Multifactor's security claims verifiable, not just marketed.

Alongside [Vivek Nair](./Vivek%20Nair.md)'s CIA cyber background, Multifactor has arguably the strongest security engineering founding pair in the YC F25/W26 cohort.

_Usage:_

"Why does zero-trust auth for AI agents need a PhD mathematician?"

"Post-quantum cryptography — which Multifactor uses — is mathematically complex. Getting the implementation wrong doesn't produce obvious errors; it produces vulnerabilities that look secure until a nation-state finds them. You want someone who can verify correctness at the proof level."

nodes.title: Tobias Herber
nodes.description: Co-founder of Metorial. 3x founder, IEEE best paper award, distributed systems and AI. Vienna.
nodes.body:
**Twitter:** @tobiasherber_ | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/tobias-herber

Co-founded [Metorial](./Metorial.md) with [Karim Rahme](./Karim%20Rahme.md). Vienna, Austria.

**3x founder**. **IEEE best paper award author** in AI/distributed systems/system software. Previously co-led technology at **Valicit** — an Abu Dhabi-based ticketing startup.

The IEEE best paper background is the technical credibility marker for building the MCP runtime layer: distributed systems reliability, sub-second cold starts, and multi-region failover require exactly the theoretical depth that produces peer-reviewed work on distributed systems.

Chose open source as the distribution strategy — the Metorial runtime is open-source, with the hosted enterprise platform as the revenue layer. The Vercel analogy he uses is precise: Vercel didn't invent deployment, it made Next.js reliable at enterprise scale. Metorial does the same for MCP.

Austria-based founding team in a Valley-dominated ecosystem: the geographic distance from the YC bubble is sometimes cited as a source of product focus rather than distraction.

_Usage:_

"Is Metorial betting on MCP specifically or on the general agent integration concept?"

"Both — but MCP is the bet. Anthropic released the protocol and the industry is converging on it. If MCP becomes the standard (signs point that way), Metorial is positioned as Vercel of that standard."

nodes.title: Skyler Chan
nodes.description: Solo founder of GRU Space, age 22. Building the first commercial lunar hotel.
nodes.body:
Founded [GRU Space](./GRU%20Space.md) solo at age 22. Currently accepting reservations for lunar hotel stays at $250K–$1M per booking.

Chan's bet is on timing: NASA's Artemis program, SpaceX's Starship, and international lunar programs are converging on a timeline where permanent human lunar presence is plausible within a decade. The hospitality and habitat layer — where humans actually live and work on the Moon — is not being built by NASA or SpaceX; it's a commercial opportunity.

The solo founder structure is notable: [GRU Space](./GRU%20Space.md) requires hardware, aerospace engineering, commercial real estate instincts, hospitality operations, and regulatory navigation. Solo founders in hardware are rare because the surface area is too large for one person. Chan's strategy likely involves extensive use of contractors, aerospace partners, and YC alumni resources.

In the W26 batch, GRU Space stood out for audacity: it's the kind of company that gets immediate press, attracts talent who want to work on a moonshot literally, and generates the Demo Day moments that put YC on news feeds.

_Usage:_

"Is GRU Space a real company or a concept?"

"Real company with actual reservation intake and habitat design work underway. Whether the timeline holds — commercial lunar hotels in the 2030s — is genuinely uncertain. But the company is operating, not just pitching."

nodes.title: Lucas Ngoo
nodes.description: Founder of Cortex AI. Building the training data layer for embodied AI and robotics.
nodes.body:
Founded [Cortex AI](./Cortex%20AI.md). Raised $6M. Ngoo's background is in computer vision and robotics data — the specific intersection needed to build high-quality embodied AI training datasets that include accurate hand and body pose annotations.

The robotics training data market is structurally similar to what Scale AI built for perception AI in autonomous vehicles: a specialized data collection and annotation pipeline that model teams don't want to build themselves. Ngoo is making the same bet that Alexandr Wang made a decade earlier, but for the embodied AI wave.

The workplace data collection angle is Cortex AI's differentiation: lab data produces policies that work in labs. Factory floor data, collected with workers doing real tasks in real environments, produces policies that generalize to deployment.

_Usage:_

"Why is embodied AI training data a separate company and not something robotics labs build internally?"

"Because the data collection, annotation, and quality assurance pipeline is a full-time operation that distracts from the actual model and hardware work. It's the same reason Scale AI exists — specialization produces better data faster."

nodes.title: Mark Pothen
nodes.description: CEO and co-founder of Beacon Health. Grew up in mother's primary care practice. 6 months embedded in a clinic before founding.
nodes.body:
**LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/mark-pothen/

Co-founded [Beacon Health](./Beacon%20Health.md) with [Obinna Akahara](./Obinna%20Akahara.md).

Grew up in his mother's primary care practice — the literal founder-market fit origin story. The pain of watching physicians spend hours on administrative tasks (prior auths, screenings, referral coordination) rather than patient care was not a problem he discovered from a case study; it was his childhood environment.

Spent **6 months embedded in a clinic implementing AI** before founding the company — not building a product, but deeply understanding the clinical workflow, EHR quirks, and physician workflow constraints that outsider founders miss.

Prior product and go-to-market roles at early-stage healthcare startups gave Pothen the commercial framework to pair with the clinical depth.

The Accel and Sequoia scout backing pre-YC signals that institutional investors already validated the team's clinical credibility before the YC program added its check — unusual for a healthcare company where clinical due diligence is longer than most YC diligence timelines.

_Usage:_

"Did Pothen go to medical school?"

"No, but the combination of growing up in primary care, 6 months embedded in a clinic, and prior healthcare startup experience gives him the clinical workflow understanding that makes the EHR integration decisions correct."

nodes.title: Obinna Akahara
nodes.description: CTO and co-founder of Beacon Health. Physics, UT Austin. Ex-LinkedIn, ex-Conversion.ai.
nodes.body:
**Twitter:** @ObinnaAka | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/obinnaakahara

Co-founded [Beacon Health](./Beacon%20Health.md) with [Mark Pothen](./Mark%20Pothen.md).

**Education:** Physics, University of Texas at Austin.

**Background:** Built production AI systems across healthcare and enterprise. Previous roles at **LinkedIn** and **Conversion.ai** (now Jasper — one of the first major AI writing tools).

The Physics undergraduate background is the systems-thinking foundation common among strong ML engineers: rigorous mathematical reasoning, comfort with uncertainty, ability to model complex systems. The LinkedIn and Conversion.ai roles give Akahara direct production AI experience at two very different scales — LinkedIn's massive data infrastructure vs Conversion.ai's early generative AI products.

The Conversion.ai/Jasper background is particularly notable: Jasper was building LLM-based products in 2020–2021, years before GPT-4 made it mainstream. Akahara's early generative AI experience means he understands the reliability and evaluation challenges of LLM-based systems from before they became fashionable.

_Usage:_

"Why does a healthcare AI CTO need a physics degree?"

"EHR system integration and AI agent reliability are complex systems problems. Physics trains the kind of rigorous reasoning about edge cases and failure modes that clinical AI requires — the same mathematical discipline, different application domain."
